definitions.explanation: A canid native to East Asia with a distinctive masked face. Not related to raccoons despite the English name. Tanuki are significant in Japanese folklore as shapeshifters.

notes:
{狸|たぬき} refers to the Japanese raccoon dog, a species unique to East Asia.

Cultural note:
The ceramic {狸|たぬき} statues with large bellies, straw hats, and sake bottles seen outside restaurants are from ⟦{信楽|しがらき}→信楽：noentry⟧ in Shiga Prefecture. In folklore, tanuki can shapeshift and are often depicted as playful tricksters, in contrast to the more cunning ⟦{狐|きつね}→狐：04337_kitsune⟧.
